transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because after these nights where I eat like that, I end up sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself. It gets so bad I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye the next morning.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during those nights?

No, I don’t feel in control. Once I take that first bite after the house gets quiet, it’s like my good sense just steps aside. I’ll be telling myself, “Belinda, stop now,” but my hands just keep reaching for more anyway.
Are these episodes of eating where you feel out of control, like you described, always at night?
I’m not really sure. The ones I notice most are at night, after everything is quiet, but I haven’t kept track well enough to say it’s always only then.
Have you noticed significant changes in your weight over time due to these episodes?
I’m not really sure. I know my weight has gone up and down some over the years, but I couldn’t say for certain it’s because of those eating nights. I haven’t been keeping close track.
During those nights, do you feel like you're eating a lot more food than you normally would in a similar period of time?

Yes. On a bad night, it’s way more than I’d normally eat. I might start with a plate of leftover casserole, and then somehow I’ve had half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is in the fridge, all in one sitting.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating?

Yes. Very guilty. I’ll sit there afterward with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel ashamed and disgusted with myself. Sometimes the next morning I can hardly pray, or look people at church in the eye.
Do you find that during these episodes of eating, you're not interested in doing other things you normally enjoy?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think about other things in the middle of it. I’m mostly just focused on eating at that point, but I can’t say I’ve noticed losing interest in my usual things exactly.
Do you find that you're eating really quickly during those episodes?

Yes, I do. I eat so fast, sometimes just standing there at the kitchen counter, that I hardly even taste what I’m eating—like pound cake or crackers. I’ve caught myself swallowing before I’ve really chewed it right.
Do you notice any physical symptoms after these episodes, like stomach pain or nausea?
Yes. I get so full it hurts. My stomach feels tight and sore, like even under my nightgown I can feel it pressing, and I have to ease myself into the recliner because moving around hurts.
Do you think you would have been interested in doing something else during those episodes of eating if it were an option?

I don’t really know. In the moment, I’m not thinking, “I’d rather be doing something else.” I’m just sort of caught up in eating. Maybe if something interrupted me I could stop, but I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Do you think about or want to do other things while you're eating during those episodes?
I’m not really sure. When it’s happening, I’m mostly just focused on the food. I don’t think I’m sitting there wishing I was doing something else. It’s more like I’m stuck in it until I stop.
Do you usually try to hide or keep secret the fact that you're eating during these episodes?

Yes… I do. At bridge or church suppers, I’ll take a small, proper-looking plate like everyone else. But then later, after people leave, I’ll go back into the kitchen and get into the leftovers where nobody can see me. It’s embarrassing, so I try to keep that part hidden.
Do you think you would be interested in doing other things if they were available to you during those episodes of eating?

I’m not sure, honestly. When it starts, I’m not really thinking about what else I could be doing. If something else was right there, maybe, but I haven’t really noticed myself wanting that in the moment.
Do these episodes of eating where you feel out of control happen to you regularly?
Yes. Since my friend passed, it’s been happening pretty regularly… usually late at night. I’d say at least once or twice most weeks, and I can’t think of a month where it really stopped or let up.
Do you think you usually start eating like this when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or upset about something?
I don’t know for sure. Sometimes I’m upset, yes, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether that’s what starts it every time. It just sort of happens, and then I’m in it.
Do you usually feel upset or emotional right before these episodes of eating start?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear feeling right before it starts. Sometimes I may be upset, but other times it just seems to happen and I don’t think about it until I’m already eating.
Do you think these episodes of eating are usually triggered by feeling upset or emotional?

I can’t really say that for sure. I know it can happen when I’m upset sometimes, but I haven’t noticed that being the usual trigger every time. Sometimes I don’t even realize what I’m feeling until it’s already happening.
Do you feel like you're not really aware of what you're eating or the taste of the food during these episodes?

Yes. A lot of the time I’m eating so fast I’m not really tasting it. I’ll be standing at the kitchen counter with pound cake or crackers, and I just keep going. Sometimes I catch myself swallowing before I’ve even really chewed it right.
Do you ever feel like you're not criticizing yourself or feeling bad about your eating while it's happening, only afterward?

Yes. While I’m doing it, I’m not really thinking bad things about myself yet. It’s afterward, when I look around and see crumbs and empty containers, that it hits me. I feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself. Some mornings after, I can hardly pray or look people at church in the eye.
